basis: Most human infections present as erysipeloid, a localized bacterial infection directly affecting skin; systemic infection and endocarditis are uncommon.
Maternal autoantibodies impair neonatal neuromuscular junction function; respiratory and feeding weakness do not establish separate lung or gastrointestinal damage.
Congenital anemia defines a blood-cell disorder; additional organ disease is not shared across this heterogeneous group.
Milk-retention cyst confined to the breast, which has no axis.
Rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia with universal limb shortening and restricted joint mobility; ptosis occurred in only 1/6 patients.
Oxidative phosphorylation defect with encephalopathy and hepatic insufficiency; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 1/2. Skeletal myopathy omitted under the four-axis cap.
Rare dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa phenotype characterized by skin atrophy, nail dystrophy and congenital sensorineural hearing impairment.
Histiocytic proliferation occupies dermis and subcutis; systemic disease is usually absent, and conjunctival or mucosal lesions are rare.
Destructive fetal brain malformation with cortical loss and severe developmental impairment; skull changes reflect reduced brain growth.
Inborn mitochondrial respiratory-chain deficiency localized to skeletal muscle.
Inherited thickening of palmoplantar epidermis; extracutaneous manifestations are subtype-specific.
Disease of the iris, an ocular structure.
Permanent tooth agenesis defines the disorder; hair abnormalities and nail dystrophy affect roughly 50–67%, supporting additional ectodermal skin involvement.
Heterogeneous single-organ umbrella includes bronchiectasis and pancreatitis; vas deferens disease has no axis. These are alternative presentations, not shared multiorgan damage.
Congenital malformation of the pulmonary valve, right ventricular outflow tract and ventricular septum; pulmonary arteries belong to cardiovascular.
Retinopathy, obesity/hypogonadism and polydactyly are defining BBS features; renal abnormalities are a major diagnostic criterion, although subtype-specific frequencies are sparse.
Medulloblastoma originates in the cerebellum; neuraxial spread remains within the neurologic axis.
Neurocutaneous DNA-repair syndrome; pigmentary retinopathy and hearing loss each >80%. Common joint contractures and dental disease omitted under the four-axis cap.
Inherited peripheral sensory nerve channelopathy causing episodic pain; no common direct damage to other organs is established.
Asymptomatic dengue virus infection; symptomatic or severe dengue organ injury cannot be assigned to this subtype.
Variant fibrinogen amyloid predominantly damages renal glomeruli; clinically significant extrarenal involvement is uncommon. Not a coagulation disorder.
Small, minimally invasive adenocarcinoma originating in lung tissue.
Benign ossifying tumor arising in the ocular choroid; bone formation does not establish a separate skeletal disorder.
Defining syndrome comprises eyelid ptosis, digit syndactyly and learning/developmental impairment, supported by the intellectual-disability parent.
Degeneration of axons and myelin distal to nerve injury; weakness reflects denervation rather than an independently defined muscle disorder.
